previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of hypertension, diabetes, migraines, and pseudotumor cerebri was admitted for recurrent severe headache and new-onset atypical chest pressure. Her blood pressure was severely elevated at 228/100 mmHg in the emergency department and responded to IV labetalol. Initial EKG showed non-specific ST-T changes, prompting concern for acute coronary syndrome, though serial troponins were negative. She had another episode of chest pressure that resolved with sublingual nitroglycerin. A nuclear stress test showed normal myocardial perfusion and left ventricular function, ruling out significant coronary artery disease. Her headaches persisted but improved with sumatriptan. Blood pressure was stabilized with the addition of lisinopril and adjustment of labetalol. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications, including aspirin for cardiovascular risk reduction, and expedited follow-up with pain management.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with headache and hypertension.  Evaluate for
acute process.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images of the head were obtained without IV
contrast.

FINDINGS:  There is no hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, shift of normally
midline structures, or acute major vascular territorial infarction. Ventricles
and sulci are mildly prominent, likely reflecting age-related atrophy.
Periventricular white matter low attenuation is compatible with chronic small
vessel ischemic disease.  Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells
are normally aerated.  Osseous structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process.

HISTORY:  ___ female with headache, hypertension, chest pain to the
back.  Evaluate for acute process.

No prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were obtained from the thoracic inlet to upper
abdomen prior to and after the administration of IV contrast.  Coronal and
sagittal reformations were obtained.

CT OF THE CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST:  The heart and pericardium are within normal
limits, without pericardial effusion.  The great vessels are within normal
limits, without a thoracic aortic dissection or pulmonary embolism within the
main pulmonary arteries or segmental branches.  Incidental note is made of a
common trunk from which the right brachiocephalic and left common carotid
artery arise.  There is no mediastinal, hilar, or axillary lymphadenopathy.

A 4-mm pulmonary nodule is present within the right upper lobe (3:17), a 3 mm
pleural-based nodule within the right minor fissure (3:47). There is a heavily
calcified nodule measuring 3 mm in the right middle lobe (3:60), likely
reflecting a calcified granuloma.

Within the right lower lobe (3:70), there is a peripherally located area of
ground glass and airspace opacity.  This may be infectious or inflammatory in
nature.  There is minimal dependent atelectases bilaterally. There is no
pleural effusion.  Limited views of the upper abdomen reveal cholecystectomy
clips.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesion is identified.
There are mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of pulmonary embolism or thoracic aortic dissection.
2.  Small focal area of airspace opacity within the right lower ___ be
infectious or inflammatory.
3.  Scattered sub 4-mm pulmonary nodules.  In the absence of risk factors for
intrathoracic malignancy, no further followup for this is necessary.
Otherwise, a followup chest CT in 12 months.
